issue_context.title: `top_k` does not preserve original row order
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

From empirical tests I did, `sort` was always implicitly maintaining the order ( when there is duplicated values on the column you sort on). For me this is a good behavior, even though I can understand it could more costly in particular in streaming mode. In this case we should add an argument `maintain_order` to allow the user to remove the randomness.

This issue is linked to this one #8410. The question behind is: Should the `sort` operation should maintain the order and can the user control this behavior?

Today, the answer to this question is not really clear and "weird" behaviors can araise. See below :




### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

(
 pl.LazyFrame({'A': [1] * 4, 'B': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']})
 .sort('A')
 .slice(0, 3)
 .collect()['B'].to_list()
) # ['D', 'B', 'C'] <- top_k does not preserve row order


(
 pl.LazyFrame({'A': [1] * 4, 'B': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']})
 .sort('A')
 .collect()
 .slice(0, 3)['B'].to_list()
) # ['A', 'B', 'C'] <- simple sort: row order in maintain
```


### Expected behavior

I think,  `sort` should have a `maintain_order` (defaulting to False, if less costly). But the user should ideally control this behavior.


### Installed versions

```
Replace this line with the output of pl.show_versions(), leave the backticks in place
```

</details>

review_comments: Now that I think of this, I think we should make a `struct` called something like `SortOptions` that implements `Default`. That should make calling this from the rust side much more ergonomic.

Are you sure that this is something for this PR?

We already have `SortOptions` (s. [here](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/polars/polars-core/src/chunked_array/ops/mod.rs#L478)) and also the possibility to [`sort_with_options`](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/polars/polars-core/src/frame/mod.rs#L1975). The difference between `sort` and `sort_with_options` is that we cannot specify multiple `descending` columns in `sort_with_options` (e.g. [this](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/9672/files/f91196b80c91f199028064d3ed98475dc53f8c2e#diff-a1f19a667bc11e4c57f3354c86ebdd7957187c45e2ff760abf857b50f8f1033dR857) is not possible with `sort_with_options`). I guess a generalization of `SortOptions` might be needed for this, but I don't see this in this PR.
The reason I propose this is because the number of arguments are becoming unwieldy and that can be resolved with an argument struct. Would you be willing to make a follow up PR on that?
Yes, already thought about that. I think I might need some guidance on how to best do this design-wise but I can do the implementation.
